# Feature checkouts

Code-ticket work runs in the checkout the session was launched from. Every
session starts from a clean, current `main`, a step that changes code works
on its feature branch, and the session ends back on `main`. Under
`coga launch` the launcher performs the branch setup and both moves; in any
other session the agent does. Ticket work creates no linked worktrees; the
one alternative checkout is the [sandbox clone fallback](sandbox-clone/SKILL.md).
Only the recurring runner's temporary control worktree and Retro's isolated
checkout (created and removed for one Retro pass) are linked worktrees; ones
left from an earlier layout are disposed of by
[coga/checkout-cleanup](../checkout-cleanup/SKILL.md).

The ticket's `## Dev` record (`branch:`, `worktree:` for a sandbox clone,
`pr:`) is the link from ticket to branch to PR. It is explicit, not inferred
from the slug, because slug conventions break whenever a PR bundles tickets,
an agent picks another branch name, or a slug is truncated. Anything that
follows the link (bump gates, `open-pr`, autoclose, retire, status views)
reads the record; a branch name need not match the slug.

`origin` and `main` stand for the configured `[git].remote` and
`[git].control_branch`; `coga/tasks/`, `coga/recurring/`, and `coga/log.md`
for the configured workspace's task, recurring, and log paths. **The Coga
roots** are the Coga root plus the configured contexts root; every eligible (unignored) file there is Coga state
that publication carries ([coga/state-publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md)).

## Leaves

- [reconciliation](reconciliation/SKILL.md) — keeping edits current with main.
- [launch-boundary](launch-boundary/SKILL.md) — preparing and returning the
  invoking checkout, refusal recovery, and exemptions.
- [chat](chat/SKILL.md) — direct chat's occupancy guard and branch.
- [manual](manual/SKILL.md) — the start, work, and end an agent performs
  when launch did not prepare the branch.
- [sandbox-clone](sandbox-clone/SKILL.md) — the sandbox clone fallback.

## Start, work, end

Main can advance during any session. Follow
[reconciliation](reconciliation/SKILL.md) for the shared freshness and conflict
policy, including documentation, ticket edits, and ad-hoc work.

### Which checkout a step starts in

The frozen step declares its entry. A workflow step may set `checkout:` to one
of four values ([definition format](../workflows/SKILL.md#definition-format)):

- `control` — run from a clean control checkout; no branch.
- `create-or-reuse` — create the task branch, or reuse the recorded one.
- `reuse-required` — reuse the recorded `branch:`; refuse without one.
- `manual` — launch prepares and returns control but sets up no branch and
  says so; the agent follows this topic itself. An omitted field means
  `manual`.

Freezing writes the explicit value on every step, so a declared policy is
authoritative: workflow name, step name, skills, a local edit of the step's
skill or section, `assignee:` and `requires:` do not change it. Customize the
procedure and its instructions freely; the checkout follows the declaration.
The field is data for the shared mechanics below and never bypasses
occupancy, Git, owner-gate or assist checks. Roles and completion gates stay
independent: a `manual` step that `requires: branch` still needs its
`branch:` before bump.

Every frozen `checkout:` value is validated before launch reserves, creates or
switches a branch; only the [launch boundary](launch-boundary/SKILL.md)'s
initial normalization to control precedes that refusal. An invalid value,
on any step, stops the launch and is a `coga validate` error. If the
ticket's workflow or step changes on control while launch prepares, launch
refuses before spawning; retry it.

The packaged workflows declare:

| Workflow | Step | `checkout:` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code/design-then-implement` | `design`, `evaluate-design`, `review-design` | `control` |
| all five packaged code/docs workflows | `implement` | `create-or-reuse` |
| `code/agent-merge`, `code/design-then-implement`, `code/with-review`, `docs/with-review` | `peer-review` | `reuse-required` |
| `code/with-self-review` | `self-qa` | `reuse-required` |
| `code/agent-merge`, `code/design-then-implement`, `code/with-review`, `docs/with-review` | `open-pr` | `control` |
| `code/with-self-review` | `pr` | `control` |
| `code/agent-merge` | `merge` | `reuse-required` |
| all but `code/agent-merge` | owner-held `review` (an explicit assist) | `reuse-required` |

Every other packaged workflow omits the field and freezes `manual`.

A repo-local copy of a workflow wins over the package. A local copy written
before `checkout:` existed therefore freezes `manual` for new tickets, even
when its name and skills match a packaged code workflow. Declare the policies
in the local definition to restore branch preparation; existing tickets keep
their snapshots.

#### Legacy snapshots

A frozen step **without** a `checkout` key was frozen before the field
existed. For those only, launch keeps the earlier closed table: the packaged
entry above applies when the qualified workflow and step match, and the
instructions the step consumes (its resolved step skill, or its live inline
`## <step>` section) equal the packaged copy. A CRLF checkout of the skill,
as Git for Windows' `core.autocrlf` produces, still matches. Older
`code/with-review` snapshots consume an inline `peer-review` section that
delegates to `code/peer-review`; both must match. Anything else gets
`manual`. The runtime notice and launch report say `legacy snapshot` when
this path selected the entry.

No command rewrites a frozen ticket to add `checkout:`. The fallback may be
deleted only in a reviewed change after no live ticket in supported repos
carries a code/docs snapshot without `checkout:`, or after an explicitly
reviewed migration of those snapshots. Do not rewrite snapshots merely to
delete it.

### In a launched session

An ordinary `coga launch` of an agent-held step (or an explicit assist on an
owner-held step) does this for every step it chains, after bringing the
checkout to current control (the [launch boundary](launch-boundary/SKILL.md)).
It sets `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` only when it will return the
checkout. The prompt's **Checkout (runtime)** notice states what it observed
and did.

1. **Entry.** For a create step with no `branch:`, launch creates one
   (`coga/<task>-<hex>`) at control and prepares `branch:` under `## Dev`.
   An ordinary agent-only startup publishes that linkage with its final
   lifecycle and launch audit before switching
   ([publication boundaries](../state-publication/launch-boundaries/SKILL.md)).
   Other managed paths retain independent linkage publication. Otherwise it reuses the first
   recorded `branch:`: a local ref as is (a behind one fast-forwards to its
   remote; ahead or diverged commits are kept and reported), or one created
   from its remote tip. It refuses — on control, starting nothing — a
   recorded branch absent everywhere, a reuse step with no branch (unless
   `## Already satisfied` evidence exists: the agent then verifies from
   control), a branch committing ticket intent control lacks ([stranded
   ticket writes](#stranded-ticket-writes)), one held by another worktree,
   or ignored files the switch would overwrite. After switching it projects
   only this ticket from control, unstaged: the session's only entry dirt.
2. **Work.** Commit only code: stage paths by name, never `git add -A` or
   `commit -a`. Never stage, commit, or restore the projected ticket. A
   context, skill, or workflow edit that belongs to the code PR is committed
   with it. Left dirty, it is
   [held for merge](../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts):
   the sweep does not publish it, and return refuses until it is committed
   on the branch or redone on control.
   To rebase, first copy the ticket outside the repo and verify the copy,
   restore it from HEAD (delete it if HEAD lacks it), rebase, then write the
   copy back unstaged and compare bytes. Test, commit, rebase onto
   `origin/main`, push.
3. **Hand off from the branch.** Write the handoff in the projected ticket,
   then run `coga bump` last; it publishes the ticket and log. Launch
   returns the checkout to a clean `main` afterwards. A bump that prints
   `[git] sync failed` or `sync refused` left the handoff unpublished, and
   launch's return will refuse over it; say so rather than discarding it.
   The bump itself was recorded, so never bump again to publish it: after a
   `sync failed`, once Git access is restored, run the `coga run
   publish-state` recovery the report prints
   ([recovery](../state-publication/SKILL.md#recovering-a-failed-publication)).
   After a `sync refused` (control's ticket changed meanwhile), preserve the
   handoff and reconcile it onto control's copy
   ([reconciliation](reconciliation/SKILL.md)). An unused prepared branch
   needs no commit or PR when the work proves already satisfied.

A control step sees `main`; publication (`coga open-pr`) reads and pushes the
branch by name from there. A step that must exceptionally change code from
control — a docs publication fix — follows the [manual procedure](manual/SKILL.md).
A preparation failure exits 75 naming the stage and where the checkout
stands; it never rolls back, and the next launch retries the same branch
name. A recorded `worktree:` (a sandbox clone) keeps this primary on control
and names the clone, which must exist on the recorded branch; see
[sandbox-clone](sandbox-clone/SKILL.md).

### Manual or API sessions, megalaunch picks, and exempt checkouts

Without the witness, and before editing in a manual-policy step, the agent
performs the start check, branch work, and end-of-step return itself, and
publishes its pre-branch ticket edits explicitly:
[coga/checkouts/manual](manual/SKILL.md).

The recorded human assist runs on its recorded PR branch under
[coga/human-assist](../human-assist/SKILL.md).

### Direct chat

`coga chat` keeps discussion and routine state edits on control, unstaged.
Before implementation or deliberately reviewed knowledge work it publishes
pending routine state, requires a clean checkout, then runs the notice's
`prepare-checkout` command; [coga/checkouts/chat](chat/SKILL.md) owns that contract.
Knowledge left dirty on the chat's branch is held for merge, and the chat's
return refuses over it.

Launch never changes directory: the session runs where `coga launch` was
invoked, and launch never follows a recorded `worktree:`.

## Which checkout you invoke Coga from

- **Mutating commands publish from wherever they run.** The exit sweep
  publishes dirty and eligible committed state under the Coga roots to
  control, even after a config failure. On a control checkout that is every
  dirty file there. On a feature or detached checkout it is routine state
  only (tickets, the log, recurring runtime state); other files, dirty or
  committed, [wait for merge](../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts).
  Write knowledge edits that should land directly on `main`; commit one that
  belongs to a code PR on its branch. Which invocations sweep is
  owned by [coga/state-publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md#when-coga-publishes).
- **`coga launch <target> --prompt-report` regenerates `.agent-skills/`.**
  It skips the state sweep. For a write-free view call
  `compose.compose_prompt_report` or `compose.compose_prompt` directly.
- **Launch and megalaunch compose from the invoking checkout.** An ordinary
  ticket launch or direct chat brings it to fresh control first (the [launch
  boundary](launch-boundary/SKILL.md)). Megalaunch fast-forwards a control
  checkout before queueing ([refresh first](../megalaunch/SKILL.md#refresh-first))
  but only fetches on a feature branch, so run it and exempt launches from a
  control checkout synced to `origin/<control>`; a stale one re-dispatches
  merged work.

## Stranded ticket writes

A ticket write committed on the feature branch strands there: control keeps
rewriting the same file at every transition. `open-pr`'s freshness gate
refuses it and `bump` warns about it on stderr. In a sandbox clone an
uncommitted ticket edit surfaces as `coga open-pr`'s "Recorded worktree has
uncommitted changes" refusal, which names this ticket's file separately.
The comparison is one-directional; a branch copy control already absorbed is
silent. Uncommitted blackboard prose left in another checkout is not
detected; publish it before switching away.

Repair: inspect the branch copy, preserve anything still needed in the primary
ticket, then restore the merge base's copy on the branch and commit:

```sh
git restore --staged --worktree --source=$(git merge-base <control> <branch>) -- <path>
```

Do not rebase to fix it, and do not restore control's copy (it goes stale at
the next transition). A dirty task/log hunk in a sandbox clone is a duplicate
only after its content is preserved in the primary ticket or verified in the
authoritative log; discard only confirmed duplicates, never commit or stash
them to pass the clean-tree gate, and never hand-edit `coga/log.md`.
This ticket's own file is never implementation diff: control has already
rewritten it, so a branch commit of it is an overlapping stranded write. Move
an intentional authored-body change to the live ticket in the primary
checkout and discard the clone's copy. `ticket.py` and other attachments
under `coga/tasks/` do not stay in the diff either: the task directory is
routine state, so a sweeping command run on the feature checkout adopts their
committed branch copies to control (the committed-state boundary in
[coga/state-publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md#control-versus-feature-checkouts)).
Make those changes in the primary checkout's live task, like an authored body
change.

Size exception: the launched lifecycle, the per-step checkout map, and the
invocation and stranded-write rules stay together because each step's
start-and-return contract needs all of them, while the procedures already
live in leaves.
"}

name: coga/checkouts/manual
description: The start check, branch work, and end-of-step return an agent performs itself when launch did not prepare its branch, and how to publish pre-branch ticket edits before switching.
---

# Manual start, work, end

Part of [coga/checkouts](../SKILL.md), which owns the launched lifecycle and
which checkout each step starts in.

## Procedure

Use this when no `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` witness is set — manual or
API sessions, megalaunch picks, exempt checkouts — and before editing in a
step whose runtime notice says launch set up no branch (manual policy, or a
control step that must exceptionally change code). The agent performs both
moves:

1. **Start check.** `git fetch origin main`, then require HEAD on `main`, a
   clean tree with Coga state included, and a successful `git merge
   --ff-only origin/main`. Launch regenerates the ignored
   `coga/.agent-skills/` view; a repo initialized before `coga init` wrote
   that ignore rule sees it as dirt — add `.agent-skills/` to
   `coga/.gitignore`, never commit it. Anything else — dirty files, another
   ticket's branch, a diverged `main` — means stop: ask the attending human,
   or `coga block` in a queue run. Do not work around an occupied checkout
   with a linked worktree, a control checkout, a stash, or a switch.
2. **Work.** Write ticket state (`branch:` under `## Dev` once created with
   `git branch <name>`, plan notes) on `main`, publish it (below), then
   switch to the feature branch and change code only; ticket edits made
   there are not published until the next sweep. A resumed branch is reused:
   switch to it and `git rebase` onto fetched `origin/main`.
3. **End.** Commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`, or
   `--force-with-lease` after a rebase), then return:
   - `git fetch origin main`;
   - for every dirty path under the Coga roots, verify it is already on
     `origin/main` by the rules of
     [the launch boundary](../launch-boundary/SKILL.md) (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <path>`;
     for `coga/log.md`, every added line is on `origin/main`) and discard it
     (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>`). `git diff`
     skips untracked files, so compare an untracked one with
     `git show origin/main:<path> | cmp - <path>` and delete it only when
     identical;
   - `git switch main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.

   If any dirty path under the Coga roots is *not* already on `origin/main`,
   or any other path is dirty, stop and escalate. A knowledge file the sweep
   [held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
   belongs in the branch's commit (or redone on `main`), not discarded. Never discard unpublished
   state. Then write the step's handoff on `main` and run `coga bump`, which
   publishes it. The session leaves the checkout on `main`, clean.

## Publish pre-branch ticket edits

Writing `branch:` or plan notes on `main` does not publish them: Git carries
uncommitted edits across a branch switch. Before switching, publish those
edits strictly, naming each edited file. The recipe resolves paths against
the current directory, which launch preserves, so anchor them at the checkout
root:

```sh
coga run publish-state "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/coga/tasks/<slug>.md"
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

Exit 0 means every named file is confirmed on control; any non-zero exit
(contract in [strict publication on
demand](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#strict-publication-on-demand))
is the stop signal. Use the status check only for dirty files you did not name,
and require it to be empty before switching. Do not fall back to calling the
sweep through a `python -c` one-liner: the sweep reports publication failures
without raising, and the shell's `python` often cannot import Coga at all. If
publication fails or the tree remains dirty, stop and escalate; do not switch,
stash, or commit the ticket edit on the feature branch. The same publication applies to a
sandbox clone's `worktree:` record in the primary checkout, before starting
work in the clone.

name: coga/checkouts/reconciliation
description: Main as the shared source of truth for all agent edits, freshness checkpoints, preserving unique work during reconciliation, and when conflicts need human judgment.
---

# Reconcile work with moving main

The configured remote control branch (`origin/main` by default) is the source of
truth for shared repository state. A local checkout and the launch prompt are
snapshots; expect main to advance during a session. This applies to all agent
edits, including code, documentation, contexts, skills, workflows, tickets,
and bootstrap or ad-hoc work. A fresh launch does not guarantee a fresh handoff.

## Freshness checkpoints

Before editing, fetch current main and inspect changes relevant to the work,
including its governing instructions. Before publishing or handing off edits,
fetch again and reconcile against that tip. Read-only work needs no merge;
qualify conclusions tied to an older revision if relevant files changed.
Git-disabled or remote-less work cannot claim remote freshness; report that
limitation when handing off changes.

## Preserve both sides

Reconciliation preserves main's newer work and the still-needed local intent:

- For committed branch work, merge or rebase current main using the owning
  workflow's procedure ([code branch procedure](../SKILL.md#start-work-end)).
  Resolve straightforward conflicts yourself; a clean Git merge still needs
  inspection for changes in meaning or assumptions.
- For uncommitted edits, inspect the branch's committed changes as well as
  its staged and unstaged deltas and main's intervening changes. Preserve the
  dirty deltas in patches or file copies, including untracked files, and
  record the original branch HEAD. Verify those backups before clearing any
  dirty files. Restore tracked files and the index from the branch's own
  HEAD, merge or rebase current main, then reapply the still-needed dirty
  deltas onto the resulting branch, resolving conflicts there. Do not replace
  a feature file with main's version first: that also removes committed
  branch work which a working-tree patch does not contain.
- For a stale ticket publication or a handoff, preserve unpublished prose
  and blackboard notes before refreshing the ticket from control. Account
  for committed local intent as well as dirty edits; reconcile the intended
  changes onto control's current ticket while respecting CLI-owned lifecycle
  fields. This ticket-specific recovery is not a recipe for replacing code
  files with main's version. Never replay a transition merely because its
  publication failed; use the publication recovery described in the
  [handoff procedure](../SKILL.md#in-a-launched-session).

If any work already landed, prove that from history and content before dropping
the duplicate. Preserve the owning definition and reconcile dependent references.

## Sync a feature branch with control

Every Coga command run from a feature or detached checkout publishes the
ticket and log it changed to control and leaves those files dirty in that
checkout by design ([state publication](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#control-versus-feature-checkouts)).
A new ticket stays untracked. That dirt blocks `git merge` or `git rebase` of
control until it is dropped.

Drop it only when every dirty or untracked file under the Coga and contexts
roots already equals control. Each such file must be a regular file whose
bytes (after clean filters) and mode equal the copy in the local
`<remote>/<control>` ref. A tracked file must also have no staged change.
`coga status` checks this against local refs (fetch first for a current
answer). When it holds, `coga status` prints the exact command, anchored to
the Git root, with paths quoted for the current shell. On POSIX it has this
shape, and any part with no paths is left out:

```bash
git --literal-pathspecs -C <root> checkout -- <tracked…> && rm -- <untracked…> && git -C <root> merge --no-edit <remote>/<control>
```

Native Windows PowerShell gets the same steps with `Remove-Item -LiteralPath`,
each nested in `if ($?) { … }`. `git merge --autostash` is not enough: it sets
aside tracked dirt, but an untracked ticket identical to control still aborts
the merge ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten"). Prefer merge
over rebase for a branch that is already pushed, so it needs no force-push.

When `coga status` instead lists files that differ, are staged, have another
mode, or are deleted, do not use the command. Publish differing routine state
(tickets, the log) first (`coga run publish-state`), then check again. A file
[held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
cannot be published from the branch: commit it on the branch for review, or
redo it on control. Otherwise reconcile those files by hand as in
[Preserve both sides](#preserve-both-sides).

## Verify and escalate

Inspect the combined diff and run checks appropriate to the affected work
after reconciliation. If publication reports that main moved again, repeat
the comparison against the new tip. Normal movement is not itself a blocker.
Escalate per session conduct when intent conflicts, ownership is unclear, or
access prevents reconciliation; identify the conflicting changes and the
decision or capability needed. Never choose main's entire file blindly,
discard unique work to silence sync, or bypass a publication or lifecycle
guard. These rules do not authorize taking over another task's dirty checkout
or crossing a human approval gate.

name: coga/knowledge
description: The permanent authoring rule for Coga knowledge — which surface owns a fact, one owner per fact, links never load content, when to attach versus cite a topic, and the topic size review policy.
---

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.

name: coga-dev/testing
description: How to run and trust Coga's test suite and validation from a checkout, the environment and fixture pitfalls, the agent-run verification tiers (no hosted CI), and the exact verification receipts reviewers expect.
---

# Testing Coga

## Commands

```sh
python -m pip install -e ".[test]"   # editable, with pytest, hatchling and pip
coga --help                          # or: python -m coga.cli --help
python -m pytest
coga validate --json                 # or: python -m coga.validate --json
```

Coga needs Python 3.11+ (`tomllib`); an older interpreter fails loud. If pip's
hash-checking mode blocks the editable install, use `uv` or prefix the one
command with `PIP_REQUIRE_HASHES=0`. A venv made with `uv venv` (or
`python -m venv --without-pip`) initially has no `pip`; `uv sync --extra test`
or `uv pip install -e ".[test]"` installs all test tools, including pip. Run
`coga validate --json` after config, workflow, or task-model changes.

**Validate `tests/fixtures/seeded-repo/coga` with `env -u SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL coga validate --json`**
when your shell exports that variable. The fixture has notifications off, and
the config-load guard rejects a bare exported `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` with no
`webhook` key (the shipped `coga.toml` notification comments). Unset the
variable for the one command; do not edit the fixture's config to satisfy it.

**A repo-wide `coga validate` refuses a shebang script that is not
executable** (`non-executable-script`); the user-facing rule, remedy, and
mode sources live in [coga/first-task](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/first-task/SKILL.md#0-check-readiness).
When adding a script under `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/`,
commit it `100755` if it starts with `#!`; import-only modules carry no
shebang and stay `100644`. A packaged-tree finding in an adopting repo is
fixed here, upstream; Dream routes it as human-needed rather than a local PR.
The walk skips symlinks and prunes `.git`, `__pycache__`, `node_modules`, and
`.venv` (`validate._check_shebang_executables`).

For artifact-level reproduction, use the
[Linux clean-install harness](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/SKILL.md). It covers current PyPI
and a wheel from `main` in a fresh Python 3.11 container, with an attended
continuation for agent login, the first-run `coga build`, and the first
ticket. The
[macOS harness on AWS](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/macos-aws/SKILL.md) runs the same walk on
an EC2 Mac dedicated host, and the
[Windows harness on AWS](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/windows-aws/SKILL.md) on EC2 Windows
Server. The
[attended human walk](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/coga/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/human-walk/SKILL.md)
is their hand-run counterpart: a first-time user installs on a fresh
`cogatest` VM while an agent records findings.

## Which code you are actually testing

- **Package-owned definitions.** Tests and harnesses read shipped skills,
  workflows and recurring definitions from the package tree
  (`src/coga/resources/templates/coga/...`). The inverse inventory in
  `test_packaging` rejects unapproved live copies, including identical ones;
  required package resources are pinned independently of local state. The
  publication regressions in `test_git` run the control tree's own imports
  and packaging/navigation/runtime checks: the first conversion uses the
  pinned Stage A merge, and final-state dirty/committed package edits must
  stay on the feature branch during a mutating CLI exit sweep. The historical
  transition test needs Git history containing that merge; a shallow checkout
  reports an explicit skip and cannot supply that transition receipt. Pass
  `--basetemp` on a roomy volume for full runs: the suite creates many
  temporary repos and can fill a small `/tmp` tmpfs. Keep that basetemp
  outside the checkout (for example a sibling directory of it): an in-checkout
  basetemp lets the missing-repo tests walk up, discover the checkout's real
  `coga.toml`, and stop testing the no-repo case (observed 2026-11-04).
  On Windows, use a short
  root such as `C:\ct`; nested control checks and wheel copies can otherwise
  exceed MAX_PATH. Control clones disable `core.autocrlf` to preserve pinned
  definition bytes. The Stage A check backports one explicit-LF test-fixture
  write; its product code and assertions remain pinned to the historical tree.

- **Run the suite with an absolute `PYTHONPATH` whenever you are not in the
  primary checkout.** In-process imports are safe: `pyproject.toml` sets
  `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["src"]`, so tests import the
  checkout's own `coga`. Subprocess children (`sys.executable -m coga.cli`,
  `coga`, `ticket.py`) inherit the environment instead, and a healthy editable
  install's `.pth` names one checkout's `src`, so without an exported absolute
  `PYTHONPATH` they run the primary checkout's package: a mixed run where
  in-process assertions exercise your branch and CLI-driven ones do not. Use
  `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src python3.12 -m pytest`. The same spelling recovers when
  the `.pth` points at a deleted worktree.
- `PYTHONPATH` must be absolute (some subprocess tests change cwd). Name a
  3.11+ interpreter explicitly; the ambient `python3` on dev machines is often
  3.9.
- **The `coga` on PATH may be a uv tool editable install**, not a checkout
  venv. Its interpreter is the `python` beside the resolved entry point:

  ```sh
  python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; from shutil import which; print(Path(which("coga")).resolve().parent / "python")'
  ```

  That environment's `coga-*.dist-info/direct_url.json` names the checkout it
  imports, regardless of your cwd. Scripts that must `import coga` against the
  active CLI run under that interpreter. Repoint it (`uv tool install --force
  -e <checkout>`; the tool env has no `pip`) only to the long-lived checkout;
  verify branches with `PYTHONPATH`. A checkout `.venv/` is the test
  environment, not what `coga` on PATH runs. If `src/coga/` edits do not show
  up, check which checkout the install imports.
- **Codex runs its commands in a login shell** (`bash -lc`), which re-reads
  `~/.profile`; one that prepends `~/.local/bin` puts the uv tool `coga` back
  in front of a checkout venv you put first on PATH before launching. To
  dogfood a branch's `coga` under codex (for example a Dream run in a scratch
  clone), set top-level `allow_login_shell = false` in that checkout's
  gitignored `.codex/config.toml` and confirm with `command -v coga` from a
  codex session.
- **Live-test a launch-path branch from a non-editable install.** To exercise
  a branch's launch, supervisor, or capture code in a real `coga launch` or
  `coga chat` session, install the branch commit non-editable into a scratch
  venv and run that venv's `coga` by absolute path (`<venv>/bin/coga launch
  ...`) without activating the venv: launch prepares the control checkout
  (`main`), so an editable install of the checkout would run main's code.
  The agent inherits the supervisor's `PATH` unchanged (`build_launch_env`
  copies the parent environment), so commands it runs inside the session (for
  example `coga mark done`) resolve the `coga` on that `PATH`. Without
  activation only the supervisor/capture side runs the branch; activating the
  venv or prepending its `bin/` would put the branch install on both sides.
  Confirm with `command -v coga` from the session, and read the results with
  that split in mind (seen in the 2026-10-15 Codex SIGINT reproduction).
- Installed-versus-source skew warnings from `launch`/`validate` are owned by
  [coga/launch](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/launch/SKILL.md).

## Test-writing rules

- Name tests after the command or module (`tests/test_launch.py`). Coga's own
  bundled ticket scripts are exercised from `tests/` against `tests/fixtures/seeded-repo/`.
- **Launch metadata is scrubbed for you.** `tests/conftest.py`
  `_clear_supervised_session_env` clears `LAUNCH_OWNED_ENV`, derived from
  `coga.task_env.TASK_ENV_KEYS`, so a worker cannot write into the outer
  launched ticket. Add new launch-owned variables to `TASK_ENV_KEYS`; do not
  add per-test `delenv` opt-outs. `tests/test_env_isolation.py` proves it.
- **Do not pin to live dogfooded state.** Files under `coga/` mutate as the
  repo is used. Strip runtime fields or freeze the period; assert structure.
- **Fixture shell scripts must be portable.** Avoid GNU-only `sed -i`,
  `readlink -f`, `date -d`; prefer Python or `sed ... > tmp && mv tmp file`.
- **Stand in for a tool interpreter with an `exec` wrapper, not a symlink.**
  Python finds `pyvenv.cfg` beside the path it was invoked by, so a symlink
  to `sys.executable` placed elsewhere runs the base interpreter without the
  venv's packages; globally installed packages then hide the loss.
  `tests/test_clean_install_harness.py` `_tool_python` writes a `/bin/sh`
  wrapper that `exec`s the quoted interpreter, and its regression test
  imports a module present only in a throwaway venv so no global package can
  stand in.
- **Native Windows fixtures use UTF-8 and LF explicitly.** `conftest` isolates
  HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA and the temp variables. Fixture
  paths are resolved to their canonical spelling, including HOME and TEMP,
  so a reused directory with different username casing matches Git's path
  reports on Windows. `init_git_repo` disables `core.autocrlf` for ordinary
  fixtures. Dedicated Git tests still exercise CRLF clean filters.
  A fresh child interpreter does not inherit pytest's monkeypatches. Launch
  fixtures that fake the supervisor inside that child must also fake the
  Windows CLI resolver there, so command planning can reach the simulated
  agent without requiring an installed agent CLI.
  `write_executable` supplies a
  Python shebang on POSIX and a `.cmd` launcher on Windows. Use
  `remove_test_checkout` when a fixture deliberately removes a Git clone;
  Git for Windows marks object files read-only.
- **All Windows exclusions use `conftest.windows_skip(reason)`.** A POSIX
  PTY-mechanics test (`pty.fork`, `TIOCSWINSZ`, SIGWINCH, fork gates) may skip
  only when its reason names the Windows-run equivalent of the same contract,
  usually in `tests/test_repl_supervisor_nt.py`. Keep
  mocked orchestration tests running; skip only actual PTY/agent behavior,
  POSIX modes or Unix host/runbook scripts, and list every non-interactive
  exclusion with its reason in the PR. Native locks and Job Object recovery
  tests must run on Windows, without externally enabling Python UTF-8 mode.
  This repository keeps `.gitignore` LF because Git for Windows can interpret
  CR-only blank ignore lines as matches; this does not change init's policy
  for adopting repositories.
- **A test that models an agent must fake one of the agent seams.** Fake
  `shutil.which` (installed agent), `subprocess.run` (the agent run), or
  `coga.launch.run_with_done_marker`. The Windows planner resolves the agent
  against the child's PATH/PATHEXT and spawns it through `ProcessTree`, so
  without a fake a native run starts the real installed `claude.exe`; native
  runs once found about 126 orchestration tests doing so. The autouse
  `tests/conftest.py` `_windows_agent_spawn_follows_test_fakes` keeps the
  bare CLI name while one of those seams is faked and routes the no-console,
  ungated Windows spawn through a faked `subprocess.run`, matching POSIX. Only
  `tests/test_repl_supervisor_nt.py`, which owns the real Windows spawn
  contract, is exempt.
- **`coga.config` and `coga.launch` share one `subprocess` module
  object.** Use one argv-dispatching mock on `coga.config.subprocess.run`.
- **Scope standard-library mocks to the operation under test.** For example,
  restore `shutil.get_terminal_size` with `monkeypatch.context()` before
  pytest reports the result; pytest also calls it with `fallback=`.
- **Symlink-loop rejection has interpreter-dependent diagnostics.** Python
  3.12 raises while resolving the cyclic contexts root; Python 3.14 leaves
  it unresolved with `strict=False`, so configuration rejects it at the
  subsequent symlink traversal check. Tests must require rejection while
  accepting either diagnostic, as `test_layout_contexts_cyclic_root_rejected`
  does.
- `hatchling` is a tracked test extra, not a runtime dependency, because
  `tests/test_packaging.py::test_wheel_includes_bootstrap_batteries` builds
  with `--no-build-isolation` and fails (not skips) without it; see
  [coga-dev/packaging](../packaging/SKILL.md). The wheel tests shell out to
  `python -m pip`, so `pip` is also an explicit test extra for uv-created
  environments that otherwise omit it.

## Known suite failures

Rule these out before blaming the change under test.

- **The full suite can exhaust `/tmp` inodes.** Each run creates thousands of
  fixture repositories. On a `/tmp` with free bytes but few free inodes, one
  run ended with 1,413 passed, 10 skipped and 2,708 errors, with 36 inodes
  left. Check `df -i /tmp`, remove only that run's fixtures, and rerun with
  `TMPDIR` on the main disk.
- **`control_relay_started` leaks between tests (open, no ticket).**
  `recurring_runner` sets the `git.control_relay_started` ContextVar when it
  relays to a control worktree, and nothing resets it between tests. Running
  `tests/test_recurring.py::test_recurring_scan_relays_into_existing_control_worktree`
  before
  `tests/test_git.py::test_recurring_all_child_retains_the_control_worktree_sweep`
  fails the second one: `_sweep_coga_state` makes no sync call
  (`assert 0 == 1`). Reproduced on control on 2026-11-02. The default
  full-suite order passes, so the failure only shows up in reordered or
  focused selections. Confirm by running the failing test alone.
- **A Windows checkout and temp directory on different drives** break
  `os.path.relpath`, which raises `ValueError` across drives. A path computed
  between package resources and a fixture repo must fall back to an absolute
  target, as `agent_skills` does for skill links. The retired hosted Windows
  runner (package on `D:`, temporary repos on `C:`) failed 228 tests this
  way; the Windows AWS harness's default layout keeps both on `C:`, so it
  does not exercise this split.

## Verification tiers and receipts

**Coga has no hosted test CI** (owner decision, 2026-11-05). Agents and the
release operator run every check on real machines. The only workflow is the
publish-only `.github/workflows/release.yml`
([coga/releasing](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/releasing/SKILL.md)).
It builds, runs `twine check` (metadata only), and uploads. It runs no tests.

History, so nobody re-adds CI without the reasons: a 2026-09-24 no-CI policy
was reversed on 2026-10-23 by PR #1097, which added a `Test` workflow running
the suite on Linux and Windows for every pull request and every push to
`main`. Automatic ticket/log publication turned that into repeated full runs,
and a packaging-twin inconsistency (live blocker-reminders template published
before its package twin) made every run fail and notify. The owner disabled
the workflow on 2026-10-26 and deleted it on 2026-11-05
(`v1/13-repair-ci-and-resume-with-release-focused-triggers`). The tradeoff:
nothing mechanical blocks a merge or an upload. Verification is a
procedure enforced by the implementer, the reviewer and the release
operator. In exchange there are no hosted runs, queues or failure
notifications, and platform checks run natively on the AWS harnesses.

**Native checks are release-only** (owner decision, 2026-11-12). Windows
and macOS full-suite receipts are required before release, not for
implementation, peer review or merge, including platform-sensitive changes.
Do not allocate native test hosts as a routine PR gate. This concentrates
native verification on the release candidate; the tradeoff is that a native
regression may first be found during release preparation and must be fixed
before tagging.

1. **Every change.** Implement, self-QA and review steps run the full suite
   locally (Linux) and record receipts.
   Record native verification as deferred to release in the PR and ticket,
   when present; Linux receipts do not provide native Windows or macOS
   evidence.
2. **Every release, before tagging.** Run the full suite at the exact commit
   to be tagged on Linux, natively on Windows through the
   [Windows AWS harness](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/windows-aws/SKILL.md#long-native-runs),
   and natively on macOS through the
   [macOS AWS harness](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/macos-aws/SKILL.md#full-suite-at-a-commit),
   plus the build, `twine check` and clean-install checks. Record the receipts
   with the release ticket. [coga/releasing](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/releasing/SKILL.md)
   owns the release procedure. A failure or missing receipt on any platform
   means no tag. A changed release commit needs new receipts; earlier PR
   receipts do not substitute for verification of that commit.

**Python 3.11 floor evidence.** At least one release suite run uses a real
Python 3.11 interpreter, Coga's `requires-python` floor. Examples are the
Linux clean-install harness's Python 3.11 container, or the Windows
harness's `checkout`, which syncs the test environment with a uv-managed
Python 3.11 (`uv sync --python 3.11 --extra test`). A green 3.12 run
is not evidence for the floor. For per-change checks, when 3.11 is unavailable,
report that gap with the actual interpreter and results. Reusable workflows
cannot assume Python 3.11 is installed in a user's environment. Raising
`requires-python` requires an owner decision.

**Receipt fields.** Each run records the full commit SHA, the platform and OS
version, the Python version, the exact command, pass/skip/fail counts, and
runtime. For example: `3f1c…` (full SHA), Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12.12,
`PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src .venv/bin/python -m pytest` -> `4058 passed, 10 skipped`
in 410s. "Tests pass" with no command and counts is not evidence. A receipt
is evidence for exactly its commit, interpreter and platform. Runs on
uncommitted changes count for a commit only when the committed tree is
identical.

**Local-run environment.** The POSIX migration-runbook test requires ripgrep
(`rg`) on PATH. Set `TERM=dumb` when output formatting matters (for example
under a forced-terminal environment), so Typer does not insert ANSI codes
into plain-text assertions. The suite does not run `coga validate`,
interactive launch (checked on EC2), or anything needing a real agent CLI,
network or AWS; such tests must skip cleanly rather than be excluded.
Windows skips about 90 more tests than Linux. The native Windows run exists
for behavior that differs there (paths, processes, locks, encoding), not for
extra Windows-only tests.

- **Verify fix claims by exact token.** A done ticket's claim that it fixed a
  failing test is not proof of what reached `main` (a half-applied fixture fix
  once stayed red for weeks while four tickets re-diagnosed it). Check with
  `git log -S'<exact token>' -- <test file>` and the absolute-`PYTHONPATH`
  run, and record a partial fix as half-applied, not absent.
- **Scope validation with `coga validate --task <slug>`.** The repo-wide run
  has no known error baseline: its last standing error sat on a draft now
  parked under `_v2/`, which validation never reads. Any repo-wide error is a
  real change, not drift to report and move on from.

## Reviewer test environment

- **`codex review`'s own test attempt is expected to fail collection** (for
  example `No module named 'tomlkit'`): it runs pytest under an ambient
  interpreter without Coga's dependencies. That is not a finding against the
  branch and does not void the review verdict. Run the suite yourself with a
  Coga-capable interpreter (`PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src .venv/bin/python -m pytest`)
  and record that command and count as the evidence.

# Manual start, work, end

Part of [coga/checkouts](../SKILL.md), which owns the launched lifecycle and
which checkout each step starts in.

## Procedure

Use this when no `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` witness is set — manual or
API sessions, megalaunch picks, exempt checkouts — and before editing in a
step whose runtime notice says launch set up no branch (manual policy, or a
control step that must exceptionally change code). The agent performs both
moves:

1. **Start check.** `git fetch origin main`, then require HEAD on `main`, a
   clean tree with Coga state included, and a successful `git merge
   --ff-only origin/main`. Launch regenerates the ignored
   `coga/.agent-skills/` view; a repo initialized before `coga init` wrote
   that ignore rule sees it as dirt — add `.agent-skills/` to
   `coga/.gitignore`, never commit it. Anything else — dirty files, another
   ticket's branch, a diverged `main` — means stop: ask the attending human,
   or `coga block` in a queue run. Do not work around an occupied checkout
   with a linked worktree, a control checkout, a stash, or a switch.
2. **Work.** Write ticket state (`branch:` under `## Dev` once created with
   `git branch <name>`, plan notes) on `main`, publish it (below), then
   switch to the feature branch and change code only; ticket edits made
   there are not published until the next sweep. A resumed branch is reused:
   switch to it and `git rebase` onto fetched `origin/main`.
3. **End.** Commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`, or
   `--force-with-lease` after a rebase), then return:
   - `git fetch origin main`;
   - for every dirty path under the Coga roots, verify it is already on
     `origin/main` by the rules of
     [the launch boundary](../launch-boundary/SKILL.md) (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <path>`;
     for `coga/log.md`, every added line is on `origin/main`) and discard it
     (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>`). `git diff`
     skips untracked files, so compare an untracked one with
     `git show origin/main:<path> | cmp - <path>` and delete it only when
     identical;
   - `git switch main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.

   If any dirty path under the Coga roots is *not* already on `origin/main`,
   or any other path is dirty, stop and escalate. A knowledge file the sweep
   [held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
   belongs in the branch's commit (or redone on `main`), not discarded. Never discard unpublished
   state. Then write the step's handoff on `main` and run `coga bump`, which
   publishes it. The session leaves the checkout on `main`, clean.

## Publish pre-branch ticket edits

Writing `branch:` or plan notes on `main` does not publish them: Git carries
uncommitted edits across a branch switch. Before switching, publish those
edits strictly, naming each edited file. The recipe resolves paths against
the current directory, which launch preserves, so anchor them at the checkout
root:

```sh
coga run publish-state "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/coga/tasks/<slug>.md"
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

Exit 0 means every named file is confirmed on control; any non-zero exit
(contract in [strict publication on
demand](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#strict-publication-on-demand))
is the stop signal. Use the status check only for dirty files you did not name,
and require it to be empty before switching. Do not fall back to calling the
sweep through a `python -c` one-liner: the sweep reports publication failures
without raising, and the shell's `python` often cannot import Coga at all. If
publication fails or the tree remains dirty, stop and escalate; do not switch,
stash, or commit the ticket edit on the feature branch. The same publication applies to a
sandbox clone's `worktree:` record in the primary checkout, before starting
work in the clone.
---
name: coga/checkouts/reconciliation
description: Main as the shared source of truth for all agent edits, freshness checkpoints, preserving unique work during reconciliation, and when conflicts need human judgment.
---

# Reconcile work with moving main

The configured remote control branch (`origin/main` by default) is the source of
truth for shared repository state. A local checkout and the launch prompt are
snapshots; expect main to advance during a session. This applies to all agent
edits, including code, documentation, contexts, skills, workflows, tickets,
and bootstrap or ad-hoc work. A fresh launch does not guarantee a fresh handoff.

## Freshness checkpoints

Before editing, fetch current main and inspect changes relevant to the work,
including its governing instructions. Before publishing or handing off edits,
fetch again and reconcile against that tip. Read-only work needs no merge;
qualify conclusions tied to an older revision if relevant files changed.
Git-disabled or remote-less work cannot claim remote freshness; report that
limitation when handing off changes.

## Preserve both sides

Reconciliation preserves main's newer work and the still-needed local intent:

- For committed branch work, merge or rebase current main using the owning
  workflow's procedure ([code branch procedure](../SKILL.md#start-work-end)).
  Resolve straightforward conflicts yourself; a clean Git merge still needs
  inspection for changes in meaning or assumptions.
- For uncommitted edits, inspect the branch's committed changes as well as
  its staged and unstaged deltas and main's intervening changes. Preserve the
  dirty deltas in patches or file copies, including untracked files, and
  record the original branch HEAD. Verify those backups before clearing any
  dirty files. Restore tracked files and the index from the branch's own
  HEAD, merge or rebase current main, then reapply the still-needed dirty
  deltas onto the resulting branch, resolving conflicts there. Do not replace
  a feature file with main's version first: that also removes committed
  branch work which a working-tree patch does not contain.
- For a stale ticket publication or a handoff, preserve unpublished prose
  and blackboard notes before refreshing the ticket from control. Account
  for committed local intent as well as dirty edits; reconcile the intended
  changes onto control's current ticket while respecting CLI-owned lifecycle
  fields. This ticket-specific recovery is not a recipe for replacing code
  files with main's version. Never replay a transition merely because its
  publication failed; use the publication recovery described in the
  [handoff procedure](../SKILL.md#in-a-launched-session).

If any work already landed, prove that from history and content before dropping
the duplicate. Preserve the owning definition and reconcile dependent references.

## Sync a feature branch with control

Every Coga command run from a feature or detached checkout publishes the
ticket and log it changed to control and leaves those files dirty in that
checkout by design ([state publication](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#control-versus-feature-checkouts)).
A new ticket stays untracked. That dirt blocks `git merge` or `git rebase` of
control until it is dropped.

Drop it only when every dirty or untracked file under the Coga and contexts
roots already equals control. Each such file must be a regular file whose
bytes (after clean filters) and mode equal the copy in the local
`<remote>/<control>` ref. A tracked file must also have no staged change.
`coga status` checks this against local refs (fetch first for a current
answer). When it holds, `coga status` prints the exact command, anchored to
the Git root, with paths quoted for the current shell. On POSIX it has this
shape, and any part with no paths is left out:

```bash
git --literal-pathspecs -C <root> checkout -- <tracked…> && rm -- <untracked…> && git -C <root> merge --no-edit <remote>/<control>
```

Native Windows PowerShell gets the same steps with `Remove-Item -LiteralPath`,
each nested in `if ($?) { … }`. `git merge --autostash` is not enough: it sets
aside tracked dirt, but an untracked ticket identical to control still aborts
the merge ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten"). Prefer merge
over rebase for a branch that is already pushed, so it needs no force-push.

When `coga status` instead lists files that differ, are staged, have another
mode, or are deleted, do not use the command. Publish differing routine state
(tickets, the log) first (`coga run publish-state`), then check again. A file
[held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
cannot be published from the branch: commit it on the branch for review, or
redo it on control. Otherwise reconcile those files by hand as in
[Preserve both sides](#preserve-both-sides).

## Verify and escalate

Inspect the combined diff and run checks appropriate to the affected work
after reconciliation. If publication reports that main moved again, repeat
the comparison against the new tip. Normal movement is not itself a blocker.
Escalate per session conduct when intent conflicts, ownership is unclear, or
access prevents reconciliation; identify the conflicting changes and the
decision or capability needed. Never choose main's entire file blindly,
discard unique work to silence sync, or bypass a publication or lifecycle
guard. These rules do not authorize taking over another task's dirty checkout
or crossing a human approval gate.
---
name: coga/knowledge
description: The permanent authoring rule for Coga knowledge — which surface owns a fact, one owner per fact, links never load content, when to attach versus cite a topic, and the topic size review policy.
---

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.
